title: Make planning a per-item pass that flags vague requests; add athena plan
summary: Retry hem1: replace default-filled plan fields with a deterministic per-item planning pass, hold back underspecified items with a named reason, and add an `athena plan` command that prints the coordinated plan. Per the user's reply, the pass reads unread requests (runs the reader) so the drain can work the queue rather than refusing them and leaving them queued. Audience is the user and the verifier judging whether the gate fires on real vague requests.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the refusal gate firing on vague requests and the plan being printed, not that fields exist.
Behavior criteria name cargo test and cargo run commands and require cited output.
New tests for each behavior; clippy and fmt --check required.
Docs and decision entry written for an outside reader.
Plan command is exercised with cargo run.
Fix the defaulting at its source in plan entry construction, and the unread-refusal deadlock in drain.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The typed request (retry hem1) governs; the introspection's proposed verifier-preflight/unverified-environment work is a separate change and is out of scope here.
The planning pass is deterministic Rust code (no model call); reading unread requests uses the existing reader step already in the drain.
Unread requests are read first (in drain and in `athena plan`), then planned from the reading; an item refused after reading is recorded with a reason and does not sit unread in the queue forever.
The earlier verifier's disk-full blocker was an environment fault, not a defect; the design of the rejected attempt is otherwise kept.
Previous finding: every behavior criterion's evidence must cite the commands that ran.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a new test shows a request with no bullets and no path-like words (e.g. 'make it better') is flagged underspecified after reading, the flag names the missing field, and the item is not in Plan::order.
Run `cargo test`: a new test shows a request's first line is no longer copied into acceptance; only explicit acceptance bullets or a reading's criteria fill it.

Run `cargo test`: a new test shows a non-proposal job's rung is inferred from its request or reading, or flagged missing; it is never silently Implementation, and an item with no determinable rung is refused.
Run `cargo test`: tests assert open_questions are filled for a read and an unread request, including a touched path that does not exist and an unresolved referenced job.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows two open items naming the same path get a dependency or different groups, and items with disjoint touches share a group.

Run `cargo test`: a drain test with RealSteps over a records fixture with one specified and one unread vague queued item shows the unread item is read by the pass (not refused merely for being unread), the vague one lands in Report::refused with a reason and is not run as a job, and the specified one runs. A further test shows an unread but specifiable request is read and then runs, so the queue does not fill with unread refused items.

Run `cargo run -- plan` (or the equivalent new command): it prints order, parallel groups, and each item's goal, rung, acceptance, open questions, dependencies, touches, plus flagged items with reasons; with nothing open it says so explicitly. The verifier's evidence cites the commands that ran and their output.

Files touched outside plan.rs, reading.rs and drain.rs (display.rs, main.rs, etc.) are named in the docs or decision entry; the docs/decisions.md tradeoff about the gate rarely firing is updated, including how unread requests are handled.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes; no secrets or personal data are added.
Docs state plainly that the planning pass is deterministic code (not a model call) and whether plan::trace/GapLog audit is wired to records or still follow-up.

out_of_scope: Verifier preflight, disk cleanup, and an 'unverified, environment' verdict state (separate change).
Calling a model inside the planning pass.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflows.
departures: Larger than the reference: ten deliverables across two crates plus a new CLI command, and the earlier attempt already cost a full cycle; the reply adds drain read-then-plan logic.
